title: ROM 2026: SRM Physiotherapy Students Complete 700 km Relay Run for a Drug-Free India
summary: Sixty-six runners from SRM College of Physiotherapy ran from Kanyakumari to Kattankulathur, reaching more than 4,000 school students with an anti-drug message.
body_html:
Chennai, 16 October 2026: The sixth edition of ROM 2026 – The Physio Run for Drug-Free India, organised by SRM College of Physiotherapy, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, has concluded at the Kattankulathur campus after a 700 km non-stop relay run from Kanyakumari.

The run brought together 66 runners and promoted fitness, collective responsibility and awareness for a drug-free India, in line with the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. It was flagged off in the presence of Kanniyakumari District Collector Mr. Pratap, IAS, the Additional Superintendent of Police, Nagercoil, and other officials.

Along the route, more than 4,000 school students took part in awareness activities and took a pledge supporting a drug-free India.

At the concluding Resonation Ceremony, Prof. C. Muthamizhchelvan, Vice Chancellor, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, said: "The real purpose of a run like this goes beyond endurance. It lies in the social message we carry to the community and the awareness we create along the way."

Prof. T. S. Veeragoudhaman, Dean, SRM College of Physiotherapy, said: "The Physio Run may have concluded today, but our social responsibility must continue."

The programme featured a visual chronicle of ROM 2026, the release of the ROM 2026 book cover and the ROM 2025 book, and recognition of the ROM team. It was organised under Prof. Veeragoudhaman as Organising Chairman, with Dr. T. N. Suresh, Vice Principal, and Dr. S. F. Mariyam Farzana, Associate Professor and Organising Secretary.
